title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to clear backlog, Musk says
detail:
Tesla extends Cybertruck production to clear backlog, Musk says
Mary Cunningham
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 12:55 PM MST 1 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Tesla is extending a deadline it set to finish Cybertruck production to give the company more time to fulfill its orders, CEO Elon Musk announced Wednesday.

In a social media post, Musk said Tesla will continue to manufacture the Cybertruck through the end of summer 2027, giving the car company a few additional months to work through its backlog. Last week, Musk originally said Tesla would wind down production by mid-2027 when he broke the Cybertruck news to customers.

Days later, he revealed Tesla would have to return some customers' deposits, noting that the Cybertruck order rate "far exceeds" the electric vehicle maker's production rate.

"We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people," he said on X.

The announcement sparked backlash from some Tesla customers on social media who said they are still waiting to get their hands on the stainless-steel pickup truck.

"Like many of you, I have a 59k Cybertruck on order," one Reddit user wrote. "I've been excited for it, and I'm getting the feeling now that it may not happen."

In his X post on Wednesday, Musk said he was extending production despite it not being the best financial decision for Tesla.

"This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what's the point?" he wrote.

title: 3 Possible Paths Forward for AI Stocks (Bull Case, Bear Case, Base Case) -- and How to Invest for Each

3 Possible Paths Forward for AI Stocks (Bull Case, Bear Case, Base Case) -- and How to Invest for Each

Artificial intelligence (AI) has become the biggest story, the central story, perhaps the only story that matters to the stock market right now. But many investors are getting anxious.

The past few months have been bad for AI stocks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 officially entered a correction (a 10% or more decline), dropping 11.3% since Oct. 6 before gaining today. That's more than halfway to a bear market (a 20% or more decline).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Some major tech names that have been driving the AI trade, such as Nvidia, CoreWeave, Tesla, Oracle, and Palantir, have seen significant share price declines over the past year.

NVDA data by YCharts

Does this mean that AI stocks are "over" and it's time to move your money to bonds or cash? Not necessarily. There are a few possible future paths for what might happen next with AI stocks and the broader stock market.

AI executives have made some incredibly lofty predictions about what their technology might do in the future. We've heard bold claims that AI will boost U.S. GDP by 50% in just four years, but also that it will replace most entry-level white-collar jobs, or even be responsible for the extinction of mankind. I'm skeptical about these most extreme scenarios.

At the other extreme, some AI skeptics believe the technology is overrated, overpriced, and unlikely to deliver meaningful gains in productivity or economic growth. I feel like this is unlikely to be true for too long. Companies across industries are experimenting with AI to improve their processes, save time, and reduce costs. Are we really supposed to believe that all that effort will amount to nothing, that AI is just going to "go away"? I doubt that.

Instead, I think it's more likely that we find a happier middle ground on the future of AI.

Let's take a big-picture look at the future of AI stocks -- with optimistic (bull case), pessimistic (bear case), and middle-ground (base case) scenarios. And let's see how you could position your investments based on which outcome you think is most likely.

Image source: Getty Images.
Bull case: Today's AI stock winners keep winning

AI doesn't destroy human civilization or take all the jobs. Instead, it delivers game-changing productivity growth. Good news comes out about a highly popular, profitable new AI product that's a game changer, like Google search was in 1999 or the iPhone in 2007. Or AI gets cheaper to build. (Or both.)

Another European country cleared Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) to offer its driver-assistance software, and electric vehicle (EV) stocks split along that line. Tesla stock is at $393.59, up 4% in afternoon trading. Finland's transport agency, Traficom, cleared the system for Finnish roads ahead of an EU-wide ruling expected in the winter months, according to Reuters.

Maja Hitij / Getty Images News via Getty Images

Lucid Group (NASDAQ:LCID) is moving the other way after Citi trimmed its price target again. Shares of Rivian Automotive (NASDAQ:RIVN) are trading slightly lower with the broader EV group.

Finland Opens Its Roads to Tesla's Driver-Assistance System

Traficom recognized the provisional type-approval that Dutch regulators issued on November 10, so Tesla can offer its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system in Finland immediately. EU-wide approval still requires a successful vote in the European Commission's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles, and Traficom said approval takes effect about three weeks after such a vote. Finland's recognition doesn't bind the country's own vote on that committee.

To win the clearance, Tesla dropped "self-driving" references from the system's name in Finnish and Swedish materials. Speed settings now reset to the limit each time the car restarts, according to the agency. Senior specialist Jukka Juhola of Traficom put responsibility directly on the motorist: "It is always the driver who receives the fine for speeding."

Retail is lining up for Anthropic

Vanda Research's Viraj Patel expects record retail buying when Anthropic (ANT) debuts. Patel puts first-day net retail buying near $250M, about twice the $118M record set by SpaceX (SPCX). He also expects around $1.4B of retail turnover on day one. ANT has no live quote yet, since it has not started trading.

How Vanda gets there

The rule of thumb: retail turnover generally runs about five times the peak day of pre-IPO perpetuals trading.

The benchmark: Vanda assumes activity follows the pattern set by SpaceX.

The rarity: only six stocks have topped $250M in a single day since 2014, with NVIDIA and Tesla accounting for almost all of them. Even for NVIDIA, $250M would be a 98th-percentile day.

For scale, $250M is about 0.4% of the up to $64.4B IPO. The $1.4B turnover is about 2.2% of it. That is arithmetic on the two figures, and it shows retail is a small slice of supply but a potentially loud one on day one.

Markets saw a sharp rotation, particularly in the largest technology stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite down about 5% and the S&P 500 down about 1%. title: Elon Musk Warns Tesla May Have to Refund Cybertruck Deposits as Production Winds Down
detail:
Elon Musk Warns Tesla May Have to Refund Cybertruck Deposits as Production Winds Down
Tesla
Jack Robbins
Wed, November 11, 2026 at 8:45 AM MST 2 min read
TSLA
Trade Tesla on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Some Tesla customers hoping to get a new cybertruck are going to be disappointed.

CEO Elon Musk says Tesla is winding down production of the popular car at its Texas factory next year and there won't be enough for everyone.

He insists the reason is because the company needs the plant to make Cybercabs instead.

He wrote on X: "The Cybertruck order rate far exceeds our production rate. We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people."

He insisted: "This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production."

Tesla

Musk did not clarify if the closure of the Texas factory meant the end of the cybertruck as a product.

Tesla

But as per the BBC, Tesla lead engineer, Wes Morrill, also appeared to suggest the vehicle was being discontinued, writing on X: "Cybertruck was an incredible technology development platform and lives on through Cybercab."

The Tesla Cybercab is an electric and driverless robotaxi which the company will now focus its efforts on in the future in terms of production.

Cybertruck had diehard fans but suffered delays in production before its 2023 release and now has declining sales figures. Prices start from $92,490.

As per The Sun, Tesla sales for the third quarter of 2026 reached 8,000 including Cybertrucks.

In 2025, Tesla sold 20,237 Cybertrucks, data from Kelley Blue Book showed.

Last year's sales showed a decrease in sales from the 38,965 sold in 2024.
